svg.aria-label: Sine-theta theorem notation: coordinate maps, rank-one geometry, Sylvester identity and spectral gap
svg.title: Sine-theta theorem: the players and how they connect
svg.desc: Deterministically constructed diagram. The coordinate spaces F, F_ex, and G embed in E through E_0, F_0, and F_1. A rank-one example shows the trial direction at 40 degrees to the wanted eigenspace and its unwanted component. The bottom panels give the residual and Sylvester identity and the exact separation delta between rho and lambda_1.

g.title: Names and types match the sine-theta section of the journal manuscript.
g.text: Trial coordinates, exact spectral coordinates, and the angle between their images
Key distinction: F, Fex, and G are coordinate spaces; their images under the frames are subspaces of E.

g.title: The three coordinate Hilbert spaces and the isometries into E.
g.text: ran(F0) ⊥ ran(F1) and ran(F0) ⊕ ran(F1) = E
Readout: X = F1 ∗E0 : F → G (unwanted exact coordinates)

g.title: Wanted horizontal eigenline, unwanted vertical eigenline, trial vector and its orthogonal projection.
g.text: |S| = sin Θ0; in this slice, |S| = sin(40°).

g.title: The residual R, unwanted-coordinate map X and their Sylvester identity.
g.text: Λ1 X − X A0 = F1 ∗ R
S = F1X; |S| = sin Θ0; δ N(sin Θ0) ≤ N(R)
Bound assumes the theorem's spectral separation, domains, and ideal membership.

g.title: A0=rho approximately 1.404, Lambda1=0.7 and delta=rho-0.7.
g.text: Here δ separates σ(A0) from σ(Λ1); it is not the
full 1.2 eigenvalue gap of the ambient operator.
